questions.question: A hall is 15 m long and 12 m broad.If the sum of the areas of the floor and the ceiling is equal to the sum of the areas of four walls, the volume(in m³) of the hall is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of hall = 15 m

Breadth of hall = 12 m

Sum of areas of floor and ceiling = Sum of areas of 4 walls

**Formula used:**

Sum of area of floor = Sum of area of ceiling = Length × Breadth

Sum of areas of 4 walls = 2 × height (length + breadth)

Volume of hall = length × breadth × height

**Calculation:**

Sum of area of floor = sum of area of ceiling = (15 × 12) m²

⇒ 180 m²

Total area of floor and ceiling = (180 + 180) m²

⇒ 360 m²

Sum of areas of 4 walls = 2H(15 + 12)

⇒ 54H

Now, according to question,

54H = 360 m²

⇒ H = 20/3 m

Volume of hall = 15 × 12 × (20/3) m³

⇒ 1200 m³

**∴ The volume of hall is 1200 m³**

questions.question: The captain of a cricket team of 11 members is 28 years old and the wicket keeper is 4 years older than him. If the ages of these two are excluded, the average age of the remaining players is two years less than the average age of the whole team. What is the average age of the team?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Age of captain = 28 years

Age of wicket keeper = 4 years older than the captain = 32 years

Average age of team without captain and wicket keeper = Average age of whole team – 2

**Formula used:**

Average age = Sum of ages of all players/Number of players

**Calculations:**

Let the sum of ages of all players is T and average age of whole team be A

⇒ A = T/11

⇒ T = 11A

Average age when captain and wicket keeper excluded = A – 2

⇒ A – 2 = (T – 28 – 32)/9

⇒ 9A – 18 = T – 60

⇒ 9A – 18 = 11A – 60

⇒ 2A = 42

⇒ A = 21

**∴**** T****he average age of the team is 21 years**

questions.question: Two numbers are respectively 25% and 50% more than a third number. The ratio of the first number to second number is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

First number = 25% more than third number

Second number = 50% more than third number 

**Calculations:**

Let the third number be 100

First number = 100 + 25% of 100

First number = (25/100) × 100 + 100

⇒ 25 + 100 = 125

Second number = 100 + 50% of 100

Second number = (50/100) × 100 + 100

⇒ 50 + 100 = 150

The ratio of first to the second number = 125 ∶ 150 ⇒ 5 ∶ 6

**∴** **The ratio of the first number to the second number is 5 ****∶**** 6**

questions.question: If a person had walked at the speed of 15 km/h instead of 10 km/h, he would have walked 25 km more.The actual distance travelled by him was:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Original speed = 10 km/hr

Imaginary speed = 15 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the time taken be T

According to question,

15T – 10T = 25

⇒ 5T = 25

⇒ T = 5 hours

Original distance travelled = (10 × 5) km

⇒ 50 km

**∴ The actual distance travelled by him was 50 km**

SP = Selling price

questions.question: Case A. In a certain store, the profit is 340% of the cost. Case B. If the cost increases by 32% but the selling price remains constant, approximately what percentage of the selling price is the profit in case B?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Profit = 340% of the cost

Increase in cost = 32%

**Formula used:**

Profit % on the cost price = (Profit/Cost price) × 100

Profit % on the selling price = (Profit/Selling price) × 100

Profit = Selling price – Cost price

**Calculations:**

Let the cost price be Rs. 100 and the selling price be SP

⇒ Profit = (SP – CP) 

Profit = 340 % of CP = Rs. 340

⇒ 340 = SP - 100

⇒ SP = Rs. 440

After increase in cost price

New cost price = 100 + (32/100) × 100 ⇒ Rs. 132

New profit = 440 – 132 ⇒ Rs. 308

Profit on the selling price = (308/440) × 100

⇒ 770/11 = 70%

**∴**** The new profit is 70% of the selling price**

questions.question: If the mean of the observations x, x + 4, x + 5, x + 7, x + 9 is 9, then the mean of the last three observations is:
questions.solution:
**Given :**

Let the total number be = 5 

Mean of the numbers = 9 

**Calculations :**

Total sum of the numbers = mean × total numbers 

⇒ 9 × 5 

⇒ 45 

So, x + x + 4 + x + 5 + x + 7 + x + 9 = 45 

⇒ 5x + 25 = 45 

⇒ x = 4 

Now the mean of the last three numbers = sum of the last three numbers/3 

sum of last three numbers = x + 5 + x + 7 + x + 9 = 33 

Mean = 33/3

⇒ 11 

∴ **Average of last 3 numbers is 11**

questions.question: A circle, with radius 8 cm, which has the area equal to the area of a triangle with base 8 cm. Then the length of the corresponding altitude of triangle is:

questions.question: A train can travel 50% faster than a car. Both start from point A at the same time and reach point B, 60 km away from point A, at the same time. On the way, however, the train lost about 12.5 min while stopping at the stations. The speed of the car is:
questions.solution:
**Given :**

Speed of train is 50% faster than car 

Distance between point A and B = 60 km

Time taken by train is to cover 60 km = (t - 12.5) minutes or (t - 12.5)/60 hours

Time taken by car to cover 60 km = t minutes or t/60 hours 

**Formula Used :**

Speed = Distance/time 

**Calculations :**

Let the speed of car be S

Speed of train is 50% more than car = S + 50% of S = (3/2)S

Now for train 

⇒ 60 = (3/2)S × (t - 12.5)/60 ...(1)

Now for car 

⇒ 60 = S × (t/60) ...(2)

Solving both equations

value of t = (75/2) minutes or (5/8) hours 

Speed of car = distance/Speed 

⇒ 60/(5/8)

⇒ 96 km/hours 

∴ **The speed of the car is 96 km/hour** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** Here, 50% = 1/2. So, Ratio of speed of train to car = 3 : 2 ⇒ 3x and 2x respectively

Now, Let the time taken by car = t hours,

Then the time taken by train = t -12.5min = t - 12.5/60 h

⇒ (t -5/24)h

Since distances are equal 

⇒ 3x × ( t - 5/24) = 2x × t

⇒ 3t - 5/8 = 2t

⇒ t = 5/8 h

Now, speed of car = Distance/Time = 60 ÷ 5/8

⇒ 60 × 8/5 = 96km/h

Earning is directly proportional to the product of the number of workers and time taken

**Calculation:**

According to question,

15 × 10 = Rs. 1800

Then, 5 × 8 = Rs. 1800 × [(5 × 8)/(15 × 10)]

questions.question: A family consists of two grandparents, three parents and four grandchildren. The average age of the grand parents is 65 years, that of the parents is 32 years and that of the grand children is 8 years. What is the average age of the family?
questions.solution:
**Given :**

Family has two grand parents, three parents and four children 

Average age of grand parents is 65 years

Average age of parents is 32 years 

Average age of grand children is 8 years

**Calculations :**

Total age of two grand parents = 65 × 2 = 130 years

Total age of three parents = 32 × 3 = 96 years 

Total age of grand children = 8 × 4 = 32 years 

Total family members = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 

Total age of family members = 130 + 96 + 32 = 258 years 

Average age of the family = (total age/total number of persons) 

⇒ 258/9 

⇒ 28(2/3)

∴ **The average age of family members = 28(2/3) years **

questions.question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 20, 40 and 80 days respectively. In how many days can A do the work if he is assisted by B and C on every third day?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete the work in = 20 days

B can complete the work in = 40 days

C can complete the work in = 80 days

**Calculations:**

A’s 1 day work = 1/20

B’s 1 day work = 1/40

C’s 1 day work = 1/80

(A + B + C)’s 1 day work = (1/20) + (1/40) + (1/80)

⇒ (4/80) + (2/80) + (1/80) = 7/80

A works for first two days and then assisted by B and C on the third day

A’s 2 day work = (1/20) × 2 = 1/10

Then the work done in 3 days = (1/10) + (7/80) ⇒ 15/80

The work done in 3 days =15/80 ⇒ 3/16

Work done in 15 days = 15/16

Remaining work = 1 – 15/16 ⇒ 1/16

On 16th and 17th day A will work alone

If A can do (1/20) work in 1 day then it will finish (1/16) work in (20/16) days

The total work will be completed in

⇒ 15 + (20/16) = 65/4 days

⇒ 65/4 days = 16.25 days

**∴**** Total work will be completed in 16.25 days or 16 days (from the options)**

questions.question: In a mixture of 60 L, the ratio of milk and water is 2 : 3, then the quantity of water in the mixture is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Quantity of mixture = 60 L

Ratio of milk and water = 2 : 3

**Calculation:**

Let the quantity of milk and water be 2x and 3x respectively

Total quantity of milk and water = 2x + 3x

⇒ 5x

According to question,

5x = 60

⇒ x = 12

Quantity of water = 3x

⇒ 3 × 12

⇒ 36 L

**∴ The quantity of water in the mixture is 36 L**
